around.headline: Thief breaks into Bengaluru PG accommodation, escapes with 12 phones and 7 laptops
around.summary: A thief broke into a paying-guest accommodation in Bengaluru and got away with 12 phones and 7 laptops, per The Times of India. If you live in a PG or shared flat, don't leave devices out in common areas or unlocked rooms, and check whether your building actually has working CCTV and secure door locks.

around.headline: AI traffic camera mistakes guitar case for helmetless pillion rider, fines Bengaluru man
around.summary: An AI-powered traffic camera in Bengaluru issued a helmet-violation challan after mistaking a guitar case strapped to a pillion seat for a helmetless passenger, per The Hindu and The Times of India. If you ever get a similarly wrong automated challan, don't ignore it or just pay it — dispute it through the traffic police's grievance channel with a photo of what was actually on your bike.
around.source: The Hindu, The Times of India

around.headline: Varthur-Gunjur corridor gets a task force as KRDCL is told to asphalt the road before flyover work
around.summary: The GBA has ordered a task force to fix Varthur-Gunjur's traffic bottlenecks, and KRDCL has been directed to asphalt Varthur Road before flyover construction begins, per The Hindu and Deccan Herald. Commuters on this corridor should expect continued disruption in the near term even as these fixes get underway.

around.headline: Bid to delete around 4,600 voters flagged in two Karnataka assembly seats
around.summary: The Times of India reports a move to delete roughly 4,600 voters' names across two Karnataka assembly constituencies during the ongoing electoral roll revision. If your name shows up on a draft deletion list, check the roll and file a correction yourself before the window closes — it won't fix itself.

around.headline: Nandini milk price hike put on hold as Karnataka CM reviews other states' pricing
around.summary: A planned hike in Nandini milk prices has been paused while the Chief Minister reviews pricing data from other states, per The Times of India. Good news for household budgets for now, but a hold isn't a cancellation — worth watching for an update.

around.headline: Maharashtra declares drought across 75% of the state amid rainfall deficit
around.summary: Maharashtra has officially declared drought conditions across three-quarters of the state due to a rainfall shortfall, per The Indian Express. Maharashtra is a major supplier of onions, pulses and cotton, so a prolonged drought there can push up vegetable and grocery prices in Bengaluru markets over the coming months.

street_smart.title: Your phone buzzes with a ₹1,000 e-challan for riding with a helmetless pillion rider — but you rode solo today, with only your guitar case bungee-corded to the pillion seat. It's exactly like today's viral Bengaluru case where an AI traffic camera mistook a guitar for a helmetless passenger. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's Bengaluru story (The Hindu, The Times of India, NDTV) about an AI-powered traffic camera issuing a helmet-violation challan after misreading a guitar case strapped to a pillion seat as a passenger.
street_smart.situation: The fine arrived as an automated SMS with a challan number and a payment link. There's no error you caused — the system just misread the shape — but the message warns of standard penalties if it's left unpaid, and there's no human on the other end of the SMS to argue with.

choices.text: Ignore the SMS — it's an obvious computer error, so it should get corrected automatically.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Bengaluru's e-challan system doesn't self-correct just because the error is obvious to you — unpaid challans sit as pending and can eventually block your RC transfer, insurance renewal or fitness certificate at the RTO once the grace period lapses. Silence is read as non-payment, not as a claim of innocence; you have to actively dispute it.

choices.text: Pay the ₹1,000 immediately online — it's easier than arguing with a machine.
choices.feedback: Risky. Paying is the fastest way to make the SMS stop, but it also legally records the violation as accepted — there's no clean way to undo an admitted challan afterward, and a padded 'violation' history can matter later if you're ever contesting a bigger case, like a disputed accident claim, where your record gets pulled up.

choices.text: Use the Bengaluru Traffic Police's e-challan portal or grievance option (or visit the traffic police station) to contest the challan, citing the challan number and a photo of what was actually on your bike.
choices.feedback: Correct. Bengaluru Traffic Police accepts disputes against wrongly issued automated challans, and a dated photo of what was really strapped to your pillion seat is exactly the evidence that gets an AI misread overturned. Keep the challan number and any timestamped photo from that ride — these misreads (guitar cases, helmets left on the seat, gas cylinders) are becoming a recurring pattern as AI enforcement expands.

choices.text: Post about it on social media and hope it goes viral like the original case did.
choices.feedback: Risky. Public attention occasionally speeds things up, but it's not a mechanism you can rely on for your own case — most wrongly fined riders never go viral, and you'd still need to file the actual dispute anyway. Virality doesn't clear a challan; a successful grievance does.

takeaways: Never ignore an e-challan you believe is wrong — dispute it within the stated window via the Bengaluru Traffic Police portal or station; left unpaid, it can block your RC transfer, insurance renewal or fitness certificate.
Keep the challan/notification number and a dated photo or video of your vehicle's actual load (guitar case, luggage, helmet on the seat) as evidence when filing a dispute against an automated fine.
Paying a wrongly issued challan to make it go away legally records it as accepted — only a formal dispute, not payment, actually clears it from your record.

quiz.why: The misread happened because the camera's detection system flagged an unusual pillion-seat shape as a passenger — a growing pattern as cities roll out AI-based automated challans.

quiz.why: The flagged deletions are part of the ongoing electoral roll revision (often called an SIR — Special Intensive Revision) that periodically updates voter lists across constituencies.

quiz.why: Maharashtra is one of India's largest producers of onions, pulses and cotton, so a prolonged drought there tends to show up nationally as price swings in these staples.

quiz.question: Who chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution, and is often called its chief architect?
quiz.why: Ambedkar's Drafting Committee produced the document that the Constituent Assembly adopted on 26 November 1949, which came into effect on 26 January 1950.

quiz.question: In economics, what does a country's 'fiscal deficit' measure?
options: The gap between the government's total expenditure and its total revenue (excluding borrowings)
The gap between exports and imports of goods
The gap between a country's savings and investments
The government's total outstanding public debt
quiz.why: A fiscal deficit is financed through borrowing, and its size relative to GDP is a key indicator of government finances tracked against targets set under the Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) framework.
